description: Baseline evaluation dataset for retrieval and grounded answer quality.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of a router?
questions.expected_answer: A router forwards packets between different networks using destination IP addresses and routing information.
evidence: A router forwards packets between different networks.
It examines destination IP addresses.

questions.question: What is the difference between a LAN and a WAN?
questions.expected_answer: A LAN connects devices over a limited geographical area, while a WAN connects networks across larger geographical distances.
evidence: A Local Area Network (LAN) connects devices within a limited geographical area.
A Wide Area Network (WAN) connects networks across larger geographical distances.

questions.question: How is a network switch different from a router?
questions.expected_answer: A switch connects devices within a local network and forwards Ethernet frames using MAC addresses. A router forwards packets between different networks using IP addresses.
evidence: A network switch connects devices within a local network.
It uses MAC addresses to forward Ethernet frames.
A router forwards packets between different networks.

questions.question: What is the purpose of DNS?
questions.expected_answer: DNS translates human-readable domain names into IP addresses.
evidence: The Domain Name System (DNS) translates human-readable domain names into IP addresses.

questions.question: What information can DHCP assign to a device?
questions.expected_answer: DHCP can assign an IP address, subnet mask, default gateway and DNS server.
evidence: This can include an IP address, subnet mask, default gateway and DNS server.

questions.question: Compare TCP and UDP in terms of reliability.
questions.expected_answer: TCP provides reliable, ordered delivery using acknowledgements, sequence numbers and retransmissions. UDP is connectionless and does not guarantee delivery, ordering or retransmission.
evidence: The Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) provides reliable, ordered delivery of data.
The User Datagram Protocol (UDP) is a connectionless transport protocol.
It has less overhead than TCP but does not guarantee delivery, ordering or retransmission.

questions.question: Which port is commonly used by HTTPS?
evidence: HTTPS commonly uses port 443.

questions.question: What are the three elements of the CIA triad?
evidence: The CIA triad is a fundamental information security model.
It consists of confidentiality, integrity and availability.

questions.question: What is the difference between authentication and authorisation?
questions.expected_answer: Authentication verifies the identity of a user or system. Authorisation determines what an authenticated identity is allowed to access.
evidence: Authentication verifies the identity of a user or system.
Authorisation determines what an authenticated identity is allowed to access.

questions.question: How can SQL injection be prevented?
questions.expected_answer: Using parameterised queries and prepared statements helps prevent SQL injection.
evidence: Parameterised queries and prepared statements help prevent SQL injection.

questions.question: What is the difference between an IDS and an IPS?
questions.expected_answer: An IDS monitors activity to identify suspicious behaviour or security incidents. An IPS can also take action to block detected malicious activity.
evidence: An intrusion detection system (IDS) monitors activity to identify suspicious behaviour.
An intrusion prevention system (IPS) can also take action to block detected malicious activity.

questions.question: Why should API keys not be committed to a public repository?
questions.expected_answer: Secrets such as API keys should be stored securely in environment variables or dedicated secret-management systems and never committed to public source repositories.
evidence: Secrets such as API keys, passwords and database credentials should be stored securely in environment variables or dedicated secret-management systems.
They should never be committed to public source repositories.

questions.question: Explain the difference between RTO and RPO.
questions.expected_answer: RTO is the maximum acceptable time to restore a service. RPO is the maximum acceptable amount of data loss measured in time.
evidence: The Recovery Time Objective (RTO) defines the maximum acceptable time to restore a service.
The Recovery Point Objective (RPO) defines the maximum acceptable amount of data loss measured in time.

questions.question: Why is a hash function not considered encryption?
questions.expected_answer: A hash function produces a fixed-length digest and is not designed to be reversed to recover the original message.
evidence: A cryptographic hash function produces a fixed-length digest from input data.
A hash is not encryption because it is not designed to be reversed to recover the original message.
